profile.name: Teoh Kai Shun
profile.oneliner: Engineer in Malaysia. Day job: keeping GPUs busy at Tencent. Nights: too many side projects. This is all of them.
profile.summary: ML Engineer at Tencent, building the platform that deploys and scales 1,000+ GPUs of model serving. First-Class CS (King's College London) and MSc Computing (AI & ML) from Imperial College London. Research in imitation learning and hyperbolic graph networks; builds models from the paper up (Transformer, SRGAN, AlphaZero-style chess) and takes them to production on Kubernetes.

nodes.title: 9Loop
nodes.what: Internship on a Svelte page generator and a game-API integration.
bullets: Learnt TypeScript in a week to refactor and extend a Svelte page generator, improving component reuse and cutting render latency by 30%.
Integrated a third-party game API and built an automated integration-test suite, raising test coverage from 40% to 85%.

nodes.title: RoboCup@Home (King's)
bullets: Implemented the speech-recognition module (Dialogflow) for natural-language commands on a service robot.
Worked on robot perception: person identification and room detection with ROS/rospy.

nodes.title: Time-of-day GPU autoscaler
nodes.tagline: GPUs that scale with the clock, fire exactly once, and never starve the cluster
nodes.what: Built from scratch on Tencent's model-serving platform: model-serving services scale their GPUs up and down on a daily schedule, on a platform 1,000+ GPUs' worth of serving runs through.
bullets: Designed and built time-of-day GPU autoscaling: schedules with conflict validation, a scheduler/executor that fires multiple configs per tick, staged two-phase scale-up, a database-enforced lock against concurrent fires, and reconciliation that auto-disables schedules whose services have gone.
Built GPU usage history (30-minute snapshots) and fixed the GPU accounting behind resource reports.
nodes.story: **Exactly-once without new infrastructure.** The scheduler runs on every replica. Redis or ZooKeeper would have been a new dependency for one feature, so a UNIQUE constraint on the execution log is the lock: one INSERT wins, the rest skip. **Scale up in two steps.** Asking a shared cluster for every GPU at once can starve other workloads or fail on the last few replicas, so scale-up takes 80% first, then the rest.

nodes.title: Cross-environment service cloning
nodes.tagline: A copy replays the service; it doesn't copy the row
bullets: Hardened cross-environment service cloning so a copy never carries the source's models, resets values on unsupported GPU types, and refuses copies made stale by a template change.
nodes.story: **The copy that broke everything.** One version refused any copy whose saved config held values the template no longer declared. Correct in principle, it broke every real copy within 24 hours. Reverted to *report* those values instead, and kept the principle.

nodes.title: Gameplay conversation query service
nodes.tagline: A new service for querying conversation data from game sessions
bullets: Since Oct 2026, second-in-command on a new Go/tRPC/Protobuf query service for gameplay-session conversation data; first fixes: timezone-wrong MySQL DATETIME writes (with a tested migration runbook) and LLM worker timeouts.

nodes.title: Multi-tenant model deployment
nodes.tagline: One platform, several business units, nobody rendering anyone else's config
nodes.what: Turned a single-tenant deployment platform into a multi-tenant one.
bullets: Made the platform multi-tenant: every query scoped by business unit with ownership checks, configuration resolved per tenant from a shared base layer, and environment tags bound to the clusters each tenant may deploy into.
nodes.story: **Don't guess who the tenant is.** Joining two request labels into a config directory resolved to a directory that doesn't exist on live traffic, and nothing reported it. Tenancy now comes from an explicit table keyed on IDs every request carries; an undeclared tenant is refused. **Don't rebuild what the platform has:** a server-side config-merge layer was rejected because the company's config system already does it, with per-tenant version pinning as a bonus.

nodes.title: Platform reliability
nodes.tagline: Tracing, self-healing cluster clients, and the guards that stop bad deploys
bullets: Request-ID tracing across every RPC, automatic rebuild of the Kubernetes client when its token expires, namespace guards before deploys, bounded cluster-probe budgets, and a migration for 29 stuck orphaned records.

Replaced N per-service detail calls with one batch call, made DAO writes transactional, removed hard-coded object-storage credentials, and led a four-phase refactor splitting monolith handlers into packages.
Wrote the platform's bilingual (English/Chinese) handover: runtime view, release and rollback, eleven recorded design decisions, runbook, known debt.

nodes.title: Acute kidney injury predictor
nodes.tagline: Flagging kidney injury from NHS blood tests, deployed and monitored on Kubernetes
nodes.what: Imperial coursework (ML systems): train a model on NHS creatinine test data, then run it as a monitored service, and handle a real failure.
bullets: Trained a gradient-boosted classifier on NHS creatinine blood-test data, reaching 87% AUC for early AKI detection.
Deployed the inference pipeline on Kubernetes with Prometheus monitoring, alerting and automated rollback on model degradation.
Wrote the postmortem for a model failure during live deployment: impact, root cause, resolution.

nodes.title: In-context imitation learning with non-Euclidean methods
nodes.tagline: Teaching a robot a task from a few demonstrations, embedding them in hyperbolic space
nodes.what: MSc research project at Imperial. It builds on Instant Policy (in-context imitation learning with graphs) and asks whether hyperbolic geometry, which suits hierarchical data, represents demonstrations better.
bullets: Designed a dual-channel architecture that embeds actions and observations separately, improving representational efficiency for few-shot imitation learning.
Developed a Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network on the Poincaré ball to capture hierarchical temporal dependencies across demonstration actions.
Proposed a Product Manifold Attention module that combines Euclidean and hyperbolic channels while keeping each geometry's relational bias.
Used Sarkar's construction for training-free hyperbolic embeddings, conditioning predictions on both demonstrations and the current observation without embedding fine-tuning.
Benchmarked against Instant Policy on robotic manipulation tasks: the baseline scored higher, and the work showed non-Euclidean methods are feasible here.
nodes.story: An honest negative result. The hyperbolic model lost to the baseline, and the write-up says so. Good material for the website: what the geometry bought, what it cost, and what I'd try next.

nodes.title: KURF research programme (King's)
nodes.tagline: Robot simulation and reinforcement learning
bullets: Built robotic manipulation simulations in CoppeliaSim/PyRep and integrated RL agents (PyTorch, TensorFlow).
Ran training, evaluation and ablations across agent architectures.

nodes.title: Neuromorphic computing (independent study)
nodes.tagline: Spiking neural networks on Intel's Loihi stack, for edge devices
bullets: Reviewed hardware and software advances in neuromorphic computing (Intel Loihi 2, Lava) for edge inference.
Implemented a winner-take-all spiking neural network in Lava for face-mask classification.

nodes.title: BlockHub
nodes.tagline: Open-source collaboration where contributors vote on-chain. Won its hackathon.
bullets: Co-designed and built a decentralised open-source collaboration platform with on-chain contributor voting and reputation; built backend and frontend. 1st place of 50+ teams at the Polygon × EasyA hackathon.

nodes.title: CarDesigner
nodes.tagline: Scan a real car with LiDAR, repaint it in 3D, park the result in your driveway in AR
bullets: Building a fully offline iOS app that scans a car with LiDAR (photogrammetry fallback), lets you design paint and livery in 3D, and shows it at real scale in AR.

nodes.title: chessAI
nodes.tagline: AlphaZero-style chess: self-play, MCTS, and a lot of GPU tuning
bullets: Implemented an AlphaZero-style chess agent from scratch: CNN board encoder, Monte-Carlo tree search, replay buffer, parallel self-play and an evaluator, then optimised self-play for the GPU.

nodes.title: Data terminal
nodes.tagline: A C++ market-data feed, streamed over a socket to a Python plotter
bullets: Wrote a C++ market-data terminal that streams live ticks from Finnhub (with a Yahoo Finance source), re-serves them over a TCP socket server, and feeds a Python live plotter.

nodes.title: expense-tracker
nodes.tagline: A keyboard-driven budget tracker in the terminal
bullets: Wrote a personal-finance TUI in Go (Bubble Tea) on pure-Go SQLite, with monthly trackings that carry budgets forward.

nodes.title: RL agent for an FPS game
nodes.tagline: An actor-critic agent learning a 3D shooter, trained across three machines
bullets: Built an RNN actor-critic agent in PyTorch for a partially observable 3D first-person environment with continuous actions.
Distributed training across 3 machines with asynchronous (A3C-style) updates, cutting wall-clock training time by about 60%.
Evaluated quantitatively (reward, episode length, policy entropy) and qualitatively (emergent behaviours).

nodes.title: iRecognise
nodes.tagline: Face recognition from motion, the neuromorphic way
bullets: Built a motion-based facial-recognition model in the neuromorphic paradigm: spiking network with reward-modulated STDP learning, plus a federated training server.

nodes.title: Wallet
nodes.tagline: Personal finance for Malaysia, read from your own bank statements, on your phone
nodes.what: An iOS app that parses Malaysian bank and card statements **on the phone**, builds a ledger, and shows what you hold and what you spent. Nothing leaves the device. Card recommendation is a later phase.
bullets: Building a Kotlin Multiplatform finance app with a SwiftUI front end; statements are parsed on-device into a local ledger and nothing leaves the phone.
The balance sheet is reconciled by replaying every movement against each statement's closing balance. A screen that can't reconcile says so instead of drawing a zero.
Enforced module boundaries in the build (Gradle rules that fail if the phone links a forbidden module), with 600+ unit tests across JVM and iOS targets.
Money is integer minor units end to end, decided and recorded on day one.
nodes.story: Statements are monthly and retrospective, so the roadmap splits into what works from statements alone and what needs live capture (bank notifications). Phase 1 shipped from real statements, and live capture is now running on an iPhone. Also: a docs tree where each leaf names the code it covers, queryable by a script, so every session reads only what it touches.

nodes.title: myBudiXc
nodes.tagline: An exchange matching engine with a batch matcher for orders that can't fill now
bullets: Built a Go exchange engine: a price-time-priority order book for instant matches, and a deadline-aware batch matcher that globally pairs unmatched orders every N minutes to maximise volume, with a WebSocket market feed.

nodes.title: Ollama home lab
nodes.tagline: My own GPU box serving local LLMs to my laptops over Tailscale
bullets: Run a private LLM serving box (Ollama on Windows + WSL) reachable from my devices over a Tailscale mesh, the default inference backend for RE-News (qwen3:32b).

nodes.title: Malaysian licence plate recognition
nodes.tagline: YOLOv8 finds the plate, a small CNN reads it
bullets: Built an end-to-end OCR pipeline for Malaysian plates: YOLOv8 detection plus a custom CNN character recogniser, 94% character-level accuracy on 2,000+ self-collected images in varied lighting.

nodes.title: polyarb
nodes.tagline: Complete-set arbitrage on Polymarket's order book
bullets: Built a Polymarket complete-set arbitrage engine: depth-aware VWAP-at-size bundle costing, live opportunity detection from the order book, and paper trading by default.
Added risk controls for non-atomic multi-leg execution, with live trading behind an explicit safety flag, plus SQLite persistence and metrics.

nodes.title: RE-News
nodes.tagline: What is Malaysia worried about right now, ranked and cited
nodes.what: Scans news, government, economic and public-opinion sources, compresses each into a common citable "signal", and has an LLM fuse only those signals into ranked, cited causal chains: "policy X led to Y, so Z feels W."
bullets: Designed a pipeline of per-source encoders (news, government, CPI/OPR/fiscal data, public opinion, search trends) that compress raw data into one citable signal schema.
Restricted the LLM to a fusion layer over signals, never raw documents, so every claim in a report resolves to its evidence.
Made the model backend switchable per stage: a local qwen3:32b on the home-lab GPU by default, Claude as an opt-in.
nodes.story: "Grey is correct": the system shows nothing rather than an extrapolation. Ties to the home lab, which the LLM runs on.

nodes.title: Sales signatures
nodes.tagline: Predicting a product's sales from products that behave like it
nodes.what: Early notes and code borrowing the Instant Policy idea: learn signature-to-signature mappings so similar products' sales histories predict a new one's.

nodes.title: SRGAN from scratch
nodes.tagline: 4× super-resolution, reproducing the paper on a Windows GPU
bullets: Implemented SRGAN from scratch in PyTorch (ResNet generator, VGG perceptual loss, adversarial training) and trained it on DIV2K at 4× upscaling, reaching 29.3 dB PSNR and 0.82 SSIM on validation.
Worked around DirectML gaps for Windows GPU training with custom replacements for unsupported operations.
Ran ablations of pixel-wise MSE vs. perceptual loss, quantifying the perceptual-quality/PSNR trade-off.

nodes.title: TradingJoe
nodes.tagline: A multi-strategy portfolio system, and the red team that retracted its own results
nodes.what: A modular portfolio system for Bursa Malaysia and US equities: Black-Litterman, Fama-French (FF3/Carhart), momentum and mean-reversion, views from analyst targets, SEC insider buys and LLM signals, and a meta-strategy blending them. Walk-forward backtests, paper and live trading via Moomoo.
bullets: Built a multi-strategy portfolio system (Black-Litterman, Fama-French, momentum, mean-reversion, a blended meta-strategy) with walk-forward backtesting and paper or live execution through Moomoo.
Added GNN and LLM view generators feeding Black-Litterman, using SEC Form 4 insider buys and analyst targets as views.

Ran a five-agent red team over my own results (leakage, finance, ML, LLM, execution), found no demonstrated out-of-sample edge, retracted the claims in writing, and disabled the affected strategy pending fixes.
nodes.story: The best story in the bank. A backtest said "5/5 beats MinVar". The red team found leakage and an LLM citing documents that had never been ingested. I published the retraction in the repo and replaced fabricated citations with an honest "no documents found". This is the one for the website.

nodes.title: Attention Is All You Need, from scratch
nodes.tagline: The original Transformer, rebuilt and trained on every season of Archer
bullets: Reimplemented the original Transformer (encoder, decoder, attention) from the paper in PyTorch, with training and evaluation scripts, and trained it on a subtitle corpus.
nodes.story: The training data is fourteen seasons of Archer subtitles. Lead with that on the website.

tencent.title: Tencent
tencent.what: The team's model-serving platform deploys, scales, health-checks and tears down GPU model-serving services on Kubernetes for several business units, safely over 1,000 GPUs' worth. I build the platform; other teams run the GPUs and the services on it. The codebase dates from 2024. I joined in March 2026, and by October I had written about 450 of its 550 commits: the GPU autoscaler, multi-tenancy, most of the reliability work and the handover. In October 2026 I started on a second service, a query service for gameplay-session conversation data.
